source: curated lyrics/song/album matches; Cover Art Archive fronts, printed wall cards as fallback
rule: A sleeve is only the real front of a verified record. Titles without a verified match stay blank jackets.

One way to lose them walking blues!.song: Diamonds on the Soles of Her Shoes
One way to lose them walking blues!.note: Official lyric: “Well, that’s one way to lose these walking blues.” 123 Last.fm plays on Graceland.

Witchi Tai To.note: Jim Pepper wrote and sang the 1969 original with Everything Is Everything. Harpers Bizarre covered it; the sleeve is the record Pepper recorded it on.

Hey Moon.album: We Must Become the Pitiless Censors of Ourselves
Hey Moon.note: Maus covering Molly Nilsson. 21 plays on this album in the collection. GPS used the title on two consecutive days.

The Predatory Wasp.song: The Predatory Wasp of the Palisades Is Out to Get Us!

Taking Tiger Mountain.note: GPS split the album title across two days. Same sleeve as “(By Strategy)”.

(By Strategy).note: Second half of the Eno title. Same sleeve as day 29.

I'll Come Running To Tie Your Shoes.note: Chorus: “I’ll come running to tie your shoe.” The song is on Another Green World (1975), not Taking Tiger Mountain (By Strategy).

Katy Song.note: The 1993 self-titled album nicknamed Rollercoaster / Red House Painters I. 10 plays in the collection.

Beyond Me, Beyond You.note: Lyric: “This goes / beyond me / beyond you.” Printed sleeve 208.

Everything That Happens.album: Everything That Happens Will Happen Today

Distant Sky.note: Track 7 of Skeleton Tree. He also has the Distant Sky Live EP printed (056); the studio album is the walking-era record.

Biscuit Town.note: Opener of The OOZ (2017), 67 plays. Not Man Alive! (printed 001, 2020, after the walk).

A Quick One While She's Away.song: A Quick One, While He's Away
A Quick One While She's Away.note: GPS has “She’s”; the 1966 mini-opera is “He’s.” Same song.

I'll Come Too.note: Assume Form was released January 2019. 13 plays in the collection.

Infant Dressing Table.note: Track 3. Later reissued as Ark; the printed card is Here Comes the Indian.
